browser_auth_strategy.decision: Server-side proxy (BFF) via Next.js Route Handlers
browser_auth_strategy.rationale: Gateway uses Bearer API key auth only (no OAuth, no mTLS, no signed agent cards). The API key MUST NOT reach the browser bundle, localStorage, or query strings (05_SECURITY §1, R02). Next.js Route Handlers run server-side and can attach the Authorization header from process.env.GENESIS_API_KEY without ever serializing it to the client.
browser_auth_strategy.alternate_rejected: Direct browser-to-gateway calls with the key in localStorage — REJECTED (R02 CRITICAL). Direct browser calls with per-user-supplied key in-memory only — REJECTED (still leaks to bundle).
browser_auth_strategy.implementation: Route Handler at /api/genesis/[...path] proxies all GET/POST to ${GENESIS_HTTP_URL}${path} with Authorization: Bearer ${GENESIS_API_KEY} attached. CORS handled by Next.js. No new identity platform introduced.

execution_mode_strategy.decision: Controlled-demo mode behind explicit nonproduction flag
execution_mode_strategy.rationale: Gateway default mode is 'development' with MemoryComputer + DEVELOPMENT_REASONING_FALLBACK. UI MUST label this honestly. Per 10_OPERATOR_DECISIONS.md, GLM may substitute for live ZAI/OpenBot in controlled reasoning; this is NOT evidence of live integration.
execution_mode_strategy.implementation: NEXT_PUBLIC_GENESIS_MODE flag: 'live' | 'controlled'. 'controlled' shows a permanent visible banner: 'Controlled test environment — not a live production provider'. Default to 'controlled' unless GENESIS_HTTP_URL points at a production-mode gateway.
execution_mode_strategy.evidence_tier_labels: E0 mock-only / E1 controlled / E2 connected engine / E3 live provider — UI labels every artifact/event with its tier.
